items.claim: I could use Tiefgarage Allee Center, Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz, Tiefgarage Friedensplatz, Tiefgarage Hotel Maritim and Tiefgarage Ulrichshaus.

items.claim: The weekday parking pattern was quietest in the small hours, usually around 03:00 to 05:00, and busiest from late morning into early afternoon, most often around 11:00 to 13:00.
items.reason: FACTS gives the family typical weekday trough at 03:00 and peak at 12:00, not the broader 03:00–05:00 and 11:00–13:00 ranges.

items.claim: Tiefgarage Ulrichshaus showed that most clearly: on weekdays it often reached 77.4% to 87.2% around midday, while weekend midday values were more often around 46.2% to 52.8%.
items.reason: FACTS reports Ulrichshaus's weekday peak as 72.5% at 11:00 and weekend effect as -15.6 points, not the quoted midday ranges.

items.claim: Weekend and weekday differences were strongest at Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz.
items.reason: The largest absolute weekend effect is Ulrichshaus at -15.6 points, while Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz is +7.8 points.

items.claim: On many weekdays it sat roughly in the 16% to 45% range through the middle of the day, but on weekends it rose much higher, including 94.9% at 12:00 and 98.5% at 17:00 on 8 August, and 100.0% at 21:00 on 15 August.
items.reason: FACTS does not contain those dated occupancies; it only reports summaries such as a 36.0% typical weekday peak at 13:00 and a monthly max of 100.0%.

items.claim: Tiefgarage Hotel Maritim was steadier than the other usable lots, usually partly full through the whole day and night.
items.reason: FACTS shows Hotel Maritim stays between 34.0% and 43.9% on a typical weekday, but it does not define or rank 'steadier than the other usable lots'.

items.claim: Compared with July, it was fuller in August at comparable night and early-morning hours: early July often sat in the mid-teens to low 30s, while August was often around 40% to 55% in those hours.
items.reason: FACTS does show a significant +13.9 point adjusted shift, but it does not contain the quoted night and early-morning ranges.

items.claim: For the other reliable lots, I did not see a clear month-to-month shift.
items.reason: The other three comparable usable lots all have no significant month-on-month change.

items.claim: I could use all 18 charging stations.
items.reason: FACTS say there were 18 stations in total, but only 15 were usable and 3 were excluded for coverage below 60%.

items.claim: Most stations were quietest overnight, then occupancy rose from late morning and stayed busiest from about 11:00 into the evening.
items.reason: The typical weekday profile bottoms out at 04:00 and peaks at 11:00, and most individual stations have overnight troughs and late-morning-to-evening peaks.

items.claim: Across the month, many stations spent long stretches at 50%, which means one of the two points was in use.
items.reason: FACTS show the usable stations have capacity 2, so 50% would mean one point in use, but they do not report how long many stations stayed at 50%.

items.claim: A few stations stayed busy for long runs.
items.reason: FACTS do not report run lengths or how long stations stayed busy.

items.claim: Hegelstraße 4 and Julius-Bremer-Straße 1 were often at 50% or 100% for hours at a time, and Breiter Weg 203 was also busy on many days.
items.reason: FACTS name these stations and show they can reach 100%, but they do not report hours-at-50/100 or how many days they were busy.

items.claim: I did not see a clear citywide weekend-versus-weekday split, and compared with July I did not see a measurable overall change.
items.reason: FACTS show mixed station-level weekend effects and mixed July-to-August changes, but they do not provide a single citywide weekend split or overall month-on-month EV metric.

items.claim: For air quality, I could use City Tunnel, Guericke Strasse, Schleinufer and West for NO2, and West for ozone.
items.reason: Those are exactly the usable NO2 and ozone series.

items.claim: NO2 followed a familiar weekday shape.
items.reason: FACTS shows a weekday profile for NO2 but not whether it was 'familiar'.

items.claim: The quietest hours were usually around 04:00 to 06:00, and the busiest were usually around 08:00 to 10:00.
items.reason: The NO2 family typical weekday profile bottoms at 04:00 and peaks at 09:00.

items.claim: Weekend values were generally lower and flatter.
items.reason: Only City Tunnel and Guericke Strasse have significant lower weekend NO2, while Schleinufer and West do not, and FACTS gives no basis for 'flatter'.

items.claim: The highest August NO2 reading was 98 µg/m³ at City Tunnel at 21:00 on 14 August.
items.reason: City Tunnel has the highest NO2 maximum at 98.0 µg/m³, recorded at 2026-08-14 21:00.

items.claim: No site reached the EU hourly limit of 200 µg/m³.
items.reason: All four NO2 sites have zero hours over the EU hourly limit.

items.claim: For the WHO daily NO2 guideline of 25 µg/m³, West stayed below it through the month.
items.reason: West has 0 days over the WHO daily NO2 guideline.

items.claim: The three traffic sites went above it on some days.
items.reason: FACTS confirms exceedances at those three other NO2 sites but does not label them as 'traffic sites'.

items.claim: Ozone at West showed the opposite daily timing from NO2.
items.reason: At West, ozone is lowest in the morning and highest in the evening, while NO2 shows the reverse timing.

items.claim: It was usually lowest in the morning, around 07:00 to 10:00, and highest from late afternoon into the evening, around 16:00 to 20:00.
items.reason: West ozone bottoms at 08:00 and peaks at 18:00, which fits those ranges.

items.claim: The highest hourly value was 173 µg/m³ at 17:00 on 15 August.
items.reason: FACTS gives West's hourly maximum as 173.0 µg/m³ but does not give 17:00 on 15 August as the time of that hourly maximum.

items.claim: I counted 10 August days above the WHO 8-hour guideline of 100 µg/m³ and 5 days above the EU 8-hour target of 120 µg/m³.
items.reason: FACTS says 15 days over the WHO 8-hour guideline and 7 days over the EU 8-hour target.

items.claim: In July, those counts were 5 and 0, so August was clearly higher for ozone.
items.reason: FACTS does not provide July threshold counts, and the month-on-month ozone change at West is not significant.

items.claim: Across NO2, I did not see a clear citywide change from July.
items.reason: FACTS shows three of four NO2 sites—City Tunnel, Guericke Strasse and West—were significantly higher than in July.

items.claim: I could rely on Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz, Tiefgarage Friedensplatz, Tiefgarage Hotel Maritim and Tiefgarage Ulrichshaus.
items.reason: These are exactly the four usable parking series.

items.claim: The clearest weekday parking pattern was in Tiefgarage Friedensplatz and Tiefgarage Ulrichshaus.
items.reason: Friedensplatz and Ulrichshaus have the two highest r_squared values and the most hours significantly different from midnight among the usable car parks.

items.claim: At Friedensplatz, the quietest part of a typical weekday was late evening, around 22:00, when it was often in the low single digits to low teens.
items.reason: Friedensplatz's typical weekday trough is at 06:00 with 6.3%, not around 22:00.

items.claim: It then climbed through the morning and was usually busiest from 11:00 to 13:00, often around 50% to 70%.
items.reason: FACTS only shows a typical weekday peak at 12:00 of 51.2%, not a verified 11:00-13:00 busiest span at 50% to 70%.

items.claim: Ulrichshaus also built up through the morning and was usually busiest around 11:00 to 13:00, commonly around 75% to 85%, before easing back toward the mid-30s late in the evening.
items.reason: Ulrichshaus peaks at 11:00 at 72.5%, below the claimed 75% to 85%, and FACTS does not give a verified 11:00-13:00 busiest span.

items.claim: Weekend and weekday use were clearly different.
items.reason: Three of the four usable parking lots have significant weekend effects.

items.claim: Friedensplatz and Ulrichshaus were much emptier on weekends than on weekdays at the same midday hours.
items.reason: Both lots have significant negative weekend effects, meaning they are emptier on weekends at the same hour.

items.claim: Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz showed the opposite pattern: many weekday daytime hours sat roughly between 20% and 45%, while weekend peaks reached 94.9% at 12:00 on 08 August and 100.0% at 21:00 on 15 August.
items.reason: FACTS has no 94.9% value or those date-times; it shows a typical weekday peak of 36.0% at 13:00 and a max of 100.0%.

items.claim: Tiefgarage Hotel Maritim followed a different shape.
items.reason: Hotel Maritim peaks overnight and bottoms out mid-afternoon, unlike the midday-peaking Friedensplatz and Ulrichshaus.

items.claim: It was often fuller late in the evening and overnight than in the middle of the day.
items.reason: Hotel Maritim's typical weekday peak is 43.9% at 04:00 and its trough is 34.0% at 16:00.

items.claim: Compared with July, it was fuller at many comparable late-evening hours.
items.reason: Hotel Maritim has a significant +13.9 point adjusted shift versus July at equal hour and weekday.

items.claim: Friedensplatz went the other way and was emptier late in the evening than in July.
items.reason: FACTS shows no significant month-to-month change at Friedensplatz; the adjusted shift is +0.8 points, not lower.

items.claim: At Ulrichshaus, I did not see a measurable month-to-month change.
items.reason: Ulrichshaus has no significant adjusted month-to-month shift.

items.reason: FACTS show 18 total stations, but only 15 were usable and 3 were excluded.

items.claim: The general pattern was steady but spread out.

items.reason: The family weekday profile reaches its trough at 04:00, which fits early morning around 04:00 to 06:00.

items.claim: Activity then built from late morning into the evening.

items.claim: Weekends leaned a bit more toward afternoon and evening use, while weekdays were more spread across working hours.
items.reason: FACTS do not include a family weekend-by-hour profile to verify this timing shift.

items.claim: Compared with July, I did not see a measurable overall change in that pattern.

items.claim: A few stations stood out for long busy stretches.

items.claim: Hegelstraße 4 also spent long runs at 50.0% or 100.0%.
items.reason: FACTS show max 100.0% and 23.4% full-occupancy time, but no run-length metric or 50.0% run statistic.

items.claim: Julius-Bremer-Straße 1 was frequently very busy as well, including many 100.0% hours from the middle of the month onward.

items.claim: I could use NO2 at City Tunnel, Guericke Strasse, Schleinufer and West, and O3 at West.

items.claim: Weekend levels were usually lower than weekday levels.

items.claim: I did not see a clear month-wide change from July.
items.reason: FACTS show three of four NO2 sites—City Tunnel, Guericke Strasse and West—were significantly higher than July.

items.claim: The EU hourly limit of 200 µg/m³ was never reached.
items.reason: All four NO2 sites have zero hours over the EU hourly limit.

items.claim: The WHO daily-mean guideline of 25 µg/m³ was exceeded on several days at City Tunnel and on some days at Schleinufer.

items.claim: I could use Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz, Tiefgarage Friedensplatz, Tiefgarage Hotel Maritim, and Tiefgarage Ulrichshaus.

items.claim: At Tiefgarage Friedensplatz and Tiefgarage Ulrichshaus, I did not see a clear month-to-month change.

items.claim: Tiefgarage Universitätsplatz followed the same shape but at a much fuller level: around 33% to 35% in the early morning, then commonly 77.9% to 86.7% between 10:00 and 12:00.
items.reason: FACTS say Universitaetsplatz had no data in this window and was not modelled.

items.claim: Weekend and weekday behaviour differed by location.
items.reason: The pooled parking model says weekend effects differed between lots.

items.claim: Tiefgarage Universitätsplatz was clearly fuller on weekdays than on weekends.
items.reason: FACTS say Universitaetsplatz had no data in this window and was not modelled.

items.claim: Its late-morning Saturday values were mostly around 44.4% to 53.2%, and Sunday values were often around 36.5% to 40.0%, well below weekday late-morning levels.
items.reason: FACTS say Universitaetsplatz had no data in this window and do not contain these hourly ranges.

items.claim: Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz showed the opposite pattern.
items.reason: FACTS show a weekend effect of +6.8 points for Elbauenpark, but significant is false, so there was no measurable opposite pattern.

items.claim: On many weekdays it stayed roughly between 15% and 52% through the day, but weekend midday values were often much higher, including 71.1% at 10:00 and 97.8% at 11:00 on 19 September, and 73.0% at 10:00 and 98.6% at 11:00 on 20 September.
items.reason: FACTS do not contain those dated hourly values, and Elbauenpark's weekend effect is not significant.

items.claim: Compared with August, the usable parking lots kept broadly the same daily shape.
items.reason: FACTS compare levels and peak hours by month but do not directly rate whether overall daily shape stayed 'broadly the same'.

items.claim: I did not see a measurable month-to-month shift in the regular weekday pattern.
items.reason: FACTS show Friedensplatz was significantly fuller than in August, with an adjusted shift of +4.1 percentage points.

items.claim: I used 17 stations.
items.reason: The EV charging quality summary shows 17 usable stations and 1 excluded station.

items.claim: The quietest hours were overnight, especially from 00:00 to 06:00, when many stations sat at 0% or 50%.
items.reason: FACTS show the weekday trough is overnight, but they do not say many stations were at 0% or 50% in that period.

items.claim: Use usually built after 07:00 and was busiest from late morning into early evening.
items.reason: The weekday median profile rises after 07:00, peaks at 11:00, and stays elevated into the evening.

items.claim: That broad shape looked much like August, so I did not see a measurable citywide shift.
items.reason: FACTS do not provide a citywide August-vs-September shift, and they actually show 4 stations significantly higher and 1 significantly lower month on month.

items.claim: Hegelstraße 4 was often full at 100%, including 00:00 to 07:00 on 16 September and 00:00 to 06:00 on 28 September.
items.reason: FACTS show Hegelstraße 4 reached 100% and was full 34.5% of known time, but not those specific date-and-hour stretches.

items.claim: Breiter Weg 203 frequently reached 100% in daytime, for example from 11:00 to 23:00 on 11 September.
items.reason: FACTS show Breiter Weg 203 reached 100% and was full 19.7% of known time, but not that specific 11 September interval.

items.claim: Liebknechtstraße 37 was one of the busiest evening sites and stayed at 100% from 17:00 to 23:00 on 8 September.
items.reason: FACTS show Liebknechtstraße 37 reached 100% and peaked at 12:00, but they do not report that 8 September evening stretch or rank it among the busiest evening sites.

items.claim: Weekdays had the clearest daytime peak.
items.reason: FACTS give a network weekday profile but no comparable network weekend profile to judge which had the clearer peak.

items.claim: On weekends I still saw busy midday and evening periods at several stations, so weekend charging was not broadly quieter.
items.reason: FACTS do not report those specific weekend midday/evening periods, and weekend effects are mixed rather than a direct network-wide 'not quieter' result.

items.claim: I could use all four NO2 sites and O3 at West.
items.reason: All 4 NO2 sites are usable, and West is the usable O3 site.

items.claim: I am not describing particles here because those sensors were not reliable enough this month.
items.reason: No PM10 or PM2.5 series were usable; all were excluded for stale readings.

items.claim: For NO2, the quietest hours were usually around 03:00 to 05:00, and the busiest periods were the daytime peaks around 07:00 to 10:00 and again from late afternoon into the evening.
items.reason: The NO2 typical weekday profile is lowest around 04:00 and is elevated around 08:00–09:00 and again in the evening.

items.claim: The highest hourly value I saw was 118 µg/m³ at City Tunnel at 18:00 on 28 September.
items.reason: City Tunnel has the highest NO2 hourly maximum at 118.0, recorded at 2026-09-28 18:00.

items.claim: That means the EU hourly limit of 200 µg/m³ was not breached.
items.reason: All four NO2 sites have 0 hours above the EU hourly limit.

items.claim: Daily mean NO2 did rise above the WHO 25 µg/m³ guideline on some days at City Tunnel, Guericke Strasse, and Schleinufer.
items.reason: Those three NO2 sites have 11, 8, and 11 days above the WHO daily guideline.

items.claim: I did not see that at West.
items.reason: West had 1 day above the WHO daily guideline.

items.claim: Compared with August, I did not see a measurable overall shift in NO2.
items.reason: NO2 shows no significant month-on-month change at any of the four sites.

items.claim: For O3 at West, the pattern was reversed: lower in the morning and highest in the late afternoon and evening.
items.reason: West O3 is lowest at 08:00 and highest at 18:00.

items.claim: The monthly maximum was 120 µg/m³ at 18:00 on 28 September.
items.reason: FACTS give West O3's monthly maximum as 120.0, but do not provide the date and time of that hourly maximum.

items.claim: I did not see any 8-hour average reach the EU target of 120 µg/m³.
items.reason: West has 0 days above the EU 8-hour target, and the worst 8-hour mean is 106.6.

items.claim: I did see 8-hour averages above the WHO 100 µg/m³ guideline late in the month, including the 14:00 to 21:00 periods on 27 and 30 September.
items.reason: FACTS show 4 days above the WHO 8-hour guideline but do not list these specific 14:00–21:00 periods or both dates.

items.claim: Ozone was lower than in August, when many afternoon hours were above 120 µg/m³.
items.reason: FACTS show West O3 was significantly lower than in August, but do not say that many August afternoon hours exceeded 120 µg/m³.

items.claim: I could use Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz, Tiefgarage Friedensplatz, Tiefgarage Hotel Maritim and Tiefgarage Universitätsplatz.
items.reason: The usable parking lots are Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz, Tiefgarage Friedensplatz, Tiefgarage Hotel Maritim and Tiefgarage Ulrichshaus; Universitaetsplatz had no data in this window.

items.claim: On weekdays, Tiefgarage Universitätsplatz showed the clearest workday shape.
items.reason: FACTS has no usable parking series named Tiefgarage Universitätsplatz; the strongest fitted weekday pattern among usable lots is Ulrichshaus (r_squared 0.787).

items.claim: It was quietest around 03:00 to 05:00, usually close to 34%, and busiest around 11:00, often around 78% to 86%.
items.reason: There is no parking series for Universitätsplatz; the usable lot Ulrichshaus bottoms at 34.4% at 04:00 and peaks at 75.0% at 11:00, not 78% to 86%.

items.claim: Tiefgarage Friedensplatz followed a similar shape: very low around 03:00 to 05:00 at 4.4% to 7.0%, then fullest in late morning, often between about 58% and 83.3%.
items.reason: FACTS gives Friedensplatz a trough of 6.5% at 03:00 and a weekday peak of 58.1% at 12:00; 4.4%, 7.0% and 83.3% are not values in FACTS.

items.claim: Weekend behaviour was very different between lots.
items.reason: The pooled test says weekend effects differ between parking lots.

items.claim: Tiefgarage Universitätsplatz was usually less full on weekend late mornings than on weekdays: many weekday 10:00 to 12:00 values were in the mid-70s to mid-80s, while Saturday 19 September reached only 45.8% at 10:00 and 49.6% at 12:00, and Sunday 20 September stayed around 36.5% to 38.2% from 11:00 to 13:00.
items.reason: Universitaetsplatz is excluded for no data, and the dated hourly values 45.8%, 49.6%, 36.5% and 38.2% are not in FACTS.

items.claim: Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz showed the opposite pattern.
items.reason: Elbauenpark's weekend effect is +6.8 points, but FACTS marks it not significant, so there is no supported opposite pattern.

items.claim: Many weekday late mornings sat roughly between 28% and 52%, but it reached 97.8% on Saturday 19 September at 11:00 and 98.6% on Sunday 20 September at 11:00.
items.reason: FACTS gives only aggregated values such as a weekday peak of 38.4% at 11:00 and a monthly max of 100.0%, not those dated 97.8% and 98.6% readings.

items.claim: Compared with August, I did not see a clear month-to-month change at Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz, Tiefgarage Friedensplatz or Tiefgarage Universitätsplatz.
items.reason: Friedensplatz was significantly higher month on month, while Universitaetsplatz was not modelled in either month.

items.claim: Their weekday shapes stayed broadly the same.
items.reason: FACTS shows Friedensplatz had a significant positive adjusted shift and Universitaetsplatz was not modelled, so this grouped claim is not supported.

items.claim: Tiefgarage Hotel Maritim changed the most inside September itself: it was still at 88.0% on 9 September at 11:00, but dropped to 0.0% on 20 September at 11:00 and then stayed mostly below 30% for several days before rising again late in the month.
items.reason: FACTS only gives Hotel Maritim's monthly min/max and typical peak/trough, not the dated 11:00 readings or the claimed several-day run below 30%.

items.claim: I could use 16 stations reliably this month.
items.reason: FACTS lists 17 usable EV charging stations this month, with 1 excluded.

items.claim: Occupancy was lowest around 03:00, rose from the morning onward, and was busiest around 11:00.
items.reason: The median weekday profile bottoms at 03:00 and peaks at 11:00, rising through the morning.

items.claim: After about 20:00, usage eased again.
items.reason: The median weekday profile declines after 20:00, from 24.7 at 20:00 to 6.9 by 23:00.

items.claim: Weekends were flatter, with more mixed daytime use and some stations carrying occupancy further into the night.
items.reason: FACTS gives per-station weekend effects but no weekend hourly profile to verify flatter or later-night use.

items.claim: Hegelstraße 4 was occupied for long stretches, often at 50% or 100%, including many night hours.
items.reason: FACTS shows mean 53.9%, full occupancy 34.5% of known time, a 05:00 trough of 37.8%, and max 100.0%, but not 'often at 50%' or 'long stretches'.

items.claim: Breiter Weg 203 was often full in daytime.
items.reason: FACTS shows a 10:00 peak of 62.6% and full occupancy 19.7% of known time, but not that it was often full specifically in daytime.

items.claim: Liebknechtstraße 37 also had many very busy weekday daytime and evening hours, including repeated 100% readings.
items.reason: FACTS shows mean 29.7%, a 12:00 peak of 44.9%, max 100.0%, and full occupancy 15.3% of known time, but not repeated 100% readings or many very busy daytime and evening hours.

items.claim: Against August, I did not see a clear overall change in the network at comparable weekday and weekend hours.
items.reason: FACTS provides month-on-month comparisons by station, but no single network-wide overall change measure.

items.claim: The daily shape looked much the same.
items.reason: FACTS does not provide a family-wide August weekday profile to compare with September's shape.

items.claim: I could use all 4 NO2 sensors and the West O3 sensor.
items.reason: All 4 NO2 sensors are usable, and West is the only usable O3 sensor.

items.claim: For NO2, the typical weekday pattern was lowest around 04:00 to 05:00 and highest around 08:00 to 10:00, with another rise later in the day at the roadside sites.
items.reason: The family NO2 weekday profile bottoms at 04:00 and peaks at 21:00, while the individual site peaks are 17:00, 22:00, 20:00 and 08:00.

items.claim: Weekends were generally less polluted than weekdays, especially in the morning.
items.reason: Only Guericke Strasse and Schleinufer have significant weekend reductions; City Tunnel and West do not, and morning-specific weekend patterns are not reported.

items.claim: At Schleinufer, many weekday 07:00 to 09:00 values were around 30 to 45, while several weekend mornings stayed in single digits or the low teens.
items.reason: FACTS do not provide Schleinufer weekday/weekend hour-by-hour NO2 values or the 07:00–09:00 ranges stated.

items.claim: I did not see any NO2 breach of the EU hourly limit of 200.
items.reason: All four NO2 sites had 0 hours above the EU hourly limit of 200.

items.claim: The highest hourly value was 118 at City Tunnel on 28 September at 18:00.
items.reason: City Tunnel reached 118 on 2026-09-28 18:00, and the other NO2 maxima were lower.

items.claim: For the WHO daily-mean guideline of 25, I saw exceedances on several days at City Tunnel, Guericke Strasse and Schleinufer.
items.reason: Those three sites had WHO daily-guideline exceedance days: 11, 8 and 11 respectively.

items.claim: At West, I did not see a daily mean above 25.
items.reason: West had 1 day above 25, with a worst daily mean of 26.1.

items.claim: For ozone at West, the highest hourly value was 120 on 28 September at 18:00.
items.reason: FACTS give the hourly maximum as 120, but the reported timestamp is for the 8-hour mean, not the hourly maximum.

items.claim: The EU 8-hour target of 120 was not exceeded.
items.reason: West had 0 days above the EU 8-hour target of 120.

items.claim: The WHO 8-hour guideline of 100 was exceeded on 27 September and 30 September.
items.reason: FACTS show 4 WHO 8-hour exceedance days and the worst on 2026-09-29, but not exceedances specifically on 27 or 30 September.

items.claim: Compared with August, high-ozone periods were less frequent: August had several 8-hour periods above 120, while September had none.
items.reason: FACTS show September ozone was significantly lower and had 0 EU 8-hour target exceedance days, but they do not report August 8-hour exceedance counts.

items.claim: I could not give a reliable PM10 or PM2.5 picture this month.
items.reason: Both PM10 and PM2.5 have no usable series this month.
